items.question: Can firm conviction arise merely from a single unsupported statement?
premises: Conviction requires adequate grounds
A single statement alone is insufficient proof
Hasty assent lacks critical examination
items.inference: One should not hastily accept a conclusion based only on a single statement.
items.plain_english: Nor should one suddenly arrive at a conviction merely on the basis of a single statement.

items.question: How can many limited atoms coexist together in a single location?
premises: Atoms are conceived as many
Material entities require distinct locations
A single place cannot contain many separate substances
items.inference: The coexistence of many atoms in one place is problematic.
uncertainties: aṇūnāṃ may refer to atomic selves rather than physical atoms
items.plain_english: And how could many atoms coexist in one and the same place?

items.question: If atoms are substantial, do their effects arise only from impressions tied to multiple existences?
premises: Substantial entities have distinct existences
Distinct existences imply separate connections
Effects would then depend on impressions linked to multiplicity
items.inference: Assuming substantiality leads to dependence on impressions arising from various separate existences.
uncertainties: saṃskārotya is an unusual form, possibly saṃskārottha
items.plain_english: If they are substantial, then what arises would be only from impressions, due to connection with various separate existences.

items.question: Does mutual pervasion among entities entail a confused pervaded-pervader relationship?
premises: Entities may be considered mutually pervading
Mutual pervasion blurs distinct roles
Blurred roles produce a pervaded-pervader relation
items.inference: Mutual pervasion would result in an entangled relation of pervaded and pervader.
items.plain_english: Because of mutual pervasion, there would arise a relation of pervaded and pervader.

items.question: How could space, intellect, mind, and similar principles abide in one place?
premises: Space, intellect, and mind are distinct principles
Distinct principles have different natures
Different natures resist co-location in one place
items.inference: The abiding of such diverse principles in one place is difficult to explain.
items.plain_english: If so, how could space, intellect, mind, and so on abide in one and the same place?

items.question: Does the established pervasiveness of all in all bodies resolve the problem of co-location?
premises: All is said to be pervasive
Pervasiveness extends to all bodies
Established pervasiveness implies presence everywhere
items.inference: The pervasiveness of all in all bodies is presented as the basis for their presence.
uncertainties: This verse may state an opponent's position or a proposed solution
items.plain_english: Because of the established pervasiveness of everything in all bodies.

items.question: Can conformity to actions explain experience without obstructing consciousness by those actions?
premises: Experiences may be attributed to conformity with actions
Actions are proposed as limiting factors
Consciousness itself would not be obstructed by actions
items.inference: If conformity to actions is the cause, consciousness is not truly obstructed by actions.
items.plain_english: If it is due to conformity with actions, then there is no obstruction of consciousness by actions.

rows.grounds: state of being a dead body

items.question: Why would a body not become a corpse if another self's manifestation abides in it?
premises: A body is considered dead without its own conscious presence
Another self's manifestation may be present in the body
Presence of another manifestation would prevent corpse-ness
items.inference: The body would not become a corpse because another self's manifestation abides there.
items.plain_english: The body would not become a corpse, because the manifestation of another self abides in it.

items.question: Would a single consciousness be overpowered by hundreds of other consciousnesses?
premises: Multiple consciousnesses may coexist
Numerical superiority could imply dominance
One consciousness might be overwhelmed by many
items.inference: In that case, one consciousness would be overpowered by hundreds of consciousnesses.
items.plain_english: Then a single consciousness would be overpowered by hundreds of consciousnesses.

items.question: Does a multiplicity of liberated beings in liberation imply multiple supreme leaders?
premises: Liberation may involve many beings identified with Shiva
Multiplicity could suggest divided sovereignty
Supreme leadership would then be fragmented
items.inference: Even in liberation, multiplicity of Shiva does not entail multiple leaders.
items.plain_english: Even in liberation, because of the multiplicity of Śivas, there would not be a multiplicity of leaders.

items.question: Why is true leadership undermined if many beings share leadership simultaneously?
premises: Leadership implies supreme authority
Many simultaneous leaders divide authority
Divided authority negates true leadership
items.inference: Even if many have leadership, the very nature of leadership is destroyed.
items.plain_english: Even if many were leaders, true leadership would be destroyed.

items.question: What constitutes the supreme and ultimate stage unlike any other state?
premises: A state may be incomparable to others
Incomparability marks supremacy
The supreme state is the ultimate stage
items.inference: That state which is like no other is the supreme, ultimate stage.
items.plain_english: That state which is like no other is the supreme, ultimate stage.

items.question: Does shared omniscience and conformity to one purpose unify all liberated beings?
premises: All may possess omniscience
Omniscient beings act in conformity with one purpose
Shared purpose implies unity
items.inference: Omniscience and conformity to one purpose establish unity among all.
items.plain_english: Because of omniscience and because all conform to one single purpose.

items.question: Is satisfaction in the supreme bliss of one's own self-glory an alternative basis for unity?
premises: Liberated beings may rest in their own self-glory
This glory is supreme bliss
Satisfaction in such bliss removes conflict
items.inference: Alternatively, unity arises from satisfaction in the supreme bliss of one's own self-glory.
items.plain_english: Or else, from satisfaction in the supreme bliss of the glory of one's own self.

items.question: Can the supreme state exist among many liberated selves while being established in beginningless Shiva?
premises: A multiplicity of liberated selves may be admitted
The supreme state remains singular in nature
That state is established in beginningless Shiva
items.inference: Even among many liberated selves, that supreme state is established in beginningless Shiva.
uncertainties: muktātmabhe is an unusual form, possibly muktātmasu or muktātmabhede
items.plain_english: Even in a multiplicity of liberated selves, that state would be established in beginningless Śiva.

rows.grounds: is found or exists as known

items.question: Why would the beginningless Shiva principle lack its own inherent joy?
premises: The Shiva principle is beginningless
A supreme principle possesses inherent joy
Denying its joy is unwarranted
items.inference: The beginningless Shiva principle must possess its own joy.
items.plain_english: Why would the beginningless Śiva principle not possess its own joy?

items.question: Does a king experience happiness while actively performing the duties of ruling?
premises: A king performs governing duties
Activity may coexist with satisfaction
Ruling can be accompanied by happiness
items.inference: Just as a king finds happiness in performing royal duties, activity need not exclude joy.
items.plain_english: Now, just as a king experiences happiness while performing the duties of ruling.

items.question: If activity and joy coexist, what prevents distinction even within liberation?
premises: The king analogy allows joy with activity
Liberation might admit analogous distinctions
No clear reason excludes distinction in liberation
items.inference: If so, then what prevents distinction even in liberation?
items.plain_english: If that is so, then what distinction is prevented even in liberation?

items.question: What kinds of faults arise from positing a multiplicity of selves?
premises: Multiplicity of selves has been examined
The examined consequences are problematic
Such problems count as faults
items.inference: Therefore, such faults arise from the doctrine of many selves.
items.plain_english: Therefore, such faults arise from the assumption of a multiplicity of selves.

items.question: Could liberation be both stainless and tainted with impurity under a multiplicity view?
premises: Liberation is defined as stainless
Multiplicity may entail residual impurity
Contradictory states cannot both hold
items.inference: Under that view, liberation would paradoxically be both stainless and with impurity.
items.plain_english: And liberation would turn out to be both stainless and tainted with impurity.

items.question: Would such contradictory possibilities arise in another philosophical view of Shiva-ness?
premises: Other views define Shiva-ness differently
Different definitions yield different consequences
Those consequences may allow contradictions
items.inference: In another view, such a possibility would arise from that form of Shiva-ness.
items.plain_english: Such a possibility would arise in another view, because of that kind of Śiva-ness.

rows.grounds: if there is unity of self
compound: ka+ādi, referring to certain principles

items.question: Does bondage and the like truly exist in oneness as opponents claim for certain principles?
premises: Opponents allege bondage exists in oneness
They cite principles such as ka and others
The allegation must be examined
items.inference: The opponent claims that in oneness bondage and such exist in principles like ka, as you say.
uncertainties: kādiṣu may refer to specific tattvas or categories beginning with ka
items.plain_english: If there is oneness, bondage and so on exist in the ka and other principles, as you, the opponent, claim.

items.question: Does simultaneous bondage and pain require a multiplicity of bodies?
premises: Bondage and pain may occur simultaneously
Multiplicity of bodies is proposed as explanation
Simultaneity does not necessarily require multiple bodies
items.inference: Simultaneous bondage and pain do not entail multiplicity of bodies.
items.plain_english: Simultaneous bondage, pain, and so on do not imply a multiplicity of bodies.

items.question: Can one reality assume various forms while many realities share one form?
premises: Unity does not exclude diverse manifestations
Multiplicity does not exclude shared essence
Form and underlying reality can be distinguished
items.inference: Even one can be of various forms, and even many can be of one form.
items.plain_english: Even one can be of various forms, and even many can be of one form.
